subject: Physics
content: Thermal energy transfer: Use of the equations Q = Pt and Q = mcΔθ to solve problems involving specific heat capacity and power.

subject: Physics
content: Ideal gases: Use of the ideal gas equation PV = nRT and the relationship between kinetic energy and temperature, E_k = (3/2)kT.

subject: Physics
content: Assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases: Volume of molecules is negligible compared to the volume of the container; collision time is negligible compared to time between collisions; collisions are elastic; negligible forces between molecules except during collisions. Derivation of pressure using Newton’s laws and momentum changes.

subject: Physics
content: Electric fields: Distribution of charge on the surface of a conductor, including the mutual repulsion of like charges (electrons).

subject: Physics
content: Capacitance: Use of the equations V = Q/(4πε₀r) and C = Q/V to determine the capacitance of an isolated charged sphere. Calculation of energy stored in a capacitor using E = (1/2)CV², E = (1/2)QV, or E = Q²/(2C).

subject: Physics
content: Electric fields: Determination of electric field strength from the gradient of a potential-distance graph.

subject: Physics
content: Accept alternative routes based on calculation of two separate energies and a difference. When no other marks awarded, credit one mark for an attempt to calculate an energy difference provided one correct energy equation seen.

subject: Physics
content: Gravitational fields: Explanation based on gravitational field strength or gravitational potential. Alternative routes for determining greater mass using null points or field line density. Calculation of radius using the formula R = √(GM/g). Representation of gravitational field lines with correct tangential arrows.

subject: Physics
content: Gravitational potential: Sketching a graph passing through specific coordinates related to gravitational potential. Explanation that the area under a gravitational potential graph represents energy transferred/work done per unit mass or change in gravitational potential.

subject: Physics
content: Gravitational forces and fields: Use of the formula F = GMm/r² to calculate the gravitational force between two masses. Calculation of resultant force and acceleration using vector addition.

subject: Physics
content: Transformers: Explanation of the role of the core in providing greater linkage of magnetic flux. Explanation of how a varying magnetic flux in the secondary coil induces an emf. Design features to improve efficiency such as using thin sheets/laminations of iron to reduce eddy currents. Explanation of the need for high voltage transmission to reduce power loss.

subject: Physics
content: Binding energy: Definition of binding energy as the energy required to separate a nucleus into its individual nucleons or energy given out when a nucleus is formed from its nucleons. Calculation of binding energy using mass defect and conversion to MeV.

subject: Physics
content: Nuclear fission and fusion: Explanation of the decay process of fission fragments, including beta-minus decay and movement towards stability on the N-Z graph.
